subject: Spike resilience program: structure & retrocharge for overages
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Kerry O'Neill <kerry@fastretail.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike resilience program: structure & retrocharge for overages

Hi Kerry,

Following our sync this morning — attached is a concise proposal for a short-duration Spike Resilience Program (SRP) to cover retail launch spikes without long-term commit changes. Key points:

- What: 48- to 72-hour temporary throughput accelerator that increases quota by a configurable multiplier (x2 or x3) for a fixed window.
- Pricing: blended surcharge at 1.6x normal per-token rate for the accelerated window.
- Credits: If usage returns to baseline within 72 hours, FastRetail receives a one-time resilience credit equal to 15% of the surcharge charged for that event.
- Retrocharge mechanics: usage beyond baseline is billed at the accelerated rate, invoiced on the next billing cycle with the applied credit if criteria met.
- Governance: max 3 SRP events per rolling 30 days without a contract amendment.

Attached: SRP-term-sheet-v1.pdf (terms + worked example).

If this structure looks acceptable I can turn it into a redlined term sheet and route for discounted approval. Would you want us to cap the absolute spend for any single SRP window?

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0187

Attachment: SRP-term-sheet-v1.pdf
From: Kerry O'Neill <kerry@fastretail.com>

Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike resilience program: structure & retrocharge for overages

Marcus — thanks for the quick write-up. A few clarifying questions before I take this to procurement:  

1) How exactly do you calculate the baseline for billing (7-day rolling avg, 30-day avg, or fixed baseline from our contract)?
2) If we proactively trigger a SRP but sustain the higher throughput beyond 72 hours, does the surcharge remain for the entire sustained period or roll into a different true-up path?
3) Can you provide an example invoice line showing the surcharge and the post-credit net amount?
4) Anything you can do on the surcharge % or the credit rate for strategic customers (we're looking to avoid a large one-time invoice hit)?

Also procurement will need an exact PO narrative and reference if we move forward.

— Kerry
Kerry O'Neill
Head of Platform Operations, FastRetail
kerry@fastretail.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike resilience program: structure & retrocharge for overages

Looping you in — FastRetail (large strategic retail account) asked for a cleaner PO narrative and wants to avoid a big one-off invoice. They asked specifically about baseline calculation and whether we can soften the surcharge / increase the resilience credit. 

Proposed commercial adjustments for approval: 
- Baseline = 30-day rolling avg (preferred by legal/finance for predictability).
- Surcharge = 1.4x (down from 1.6x) for x2 accelerator; 1.8x for x3.
- Resilience credit = 20% of surcharge for events closed within 72 hours.
- Per-event hard cap = $35k net charge to FastRetail (Redwood covers beyond cap for goodwill once per contract year).

Thoughts? If we agree I can redline the sheet and request a temporary pricing override (internal approval) for this account.

- Marcus

Marcus — high level: I like the SRP as a productized short-term uplift. Approve the reduced surcharge to 1.45x for x2 accelerator (compromise). Approve resilience credit at 18%. Approve a per-event cap of $30k net charge for FastRetail (Redwood will cost-share above that once per contract year). 

Conditions:  
- Baseline must be explicitly defined in the term sheet as 30-day rolling average with a 3-day lookback protection for launch volatility.
- Add language: if customer sustains >72 hours we automatically convert the window to a temporary commit amendment and charge the standard committed rate for the incremental usage beyond 72 hours (invoice in next cycle).

If legal is ok with the wording, I'm good to greenlight. Ben — can you confirm this still leaves us acceptable margin? Karthik — ops: can your teams implement the 3-day lookback and auto-convert flow?

Thanks,
Lauren

Kerry — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear procurement note. Per internal review we've updated the SRP as discussed and attached SRP-term-sheet-v2-redlined.pdf with final commercial terms: 

- Baseline: 30-day rolling average; 3-day lookback guard for launch volatility.
- Accelerator options: x2 (1.45x surcharge), x3 (1.85x surcharge).
- Resilience credit: 18% applied to the surcharge if usage returns to baseline within 72 hours.
- Per-event net cap: $30,000 (Redwood cost-shares amounts above cap once per contract year).
- Auto-convert: events sustained >72 hours convert to temporary commit at committed rates for incremental usage.

Example invoice line (worked example in the redline):
- Baseline daily tokens: 12M
- Event usage (48h, x2 window): additional 12M tokens charged at 1.45x => surcharge portion $X.
- Resilience credit (if returned): 18% of surcharge => credit $Y.

If FastRetail signs PO referencing deal FR-2023-1192 and attaches the PO to the DocuSign envelope (link below), we'll apply a one-time launch smoothing credit of $10,000 on the first SRP event.
